about: How each state counts, for F4 and F5, editorial. Keyed by state postal. counting: one or two sentences; expect: when meaningful results usually arrive; note: anything else.

NE.counting: Early and mail ballots are counted first and reported soon after polls close; election-day precincts follow through the evening.
NE.expect: Most of the vote within two hours of poll close; Douglas County (Omaha) can run later.

MT.counting: Absentee ballots, which are most of the vote, are counted on election day and reported early; election-day totals follow.
MT.expect: Half the vote by midnight Eastern; rural counties can take until morning.

ID.counting: Counties report precinct totals through the night; Ada County (Boise) reports in batches.
ID.expect: Most of the vote by 1 a.m. Eastern.

SD.counting: Precinct totals through the night; small counties finish quickly.

CA.counting: Mail ballots postmarked by election day count if they arrive within seven days, so the count continues for weeks; election-night totals are partial.
CA.expect: Early mail results right after poll close, then slow updates for days.

AK.counting: First choices are reported on election night; the ranked-choice tabulation happens about two weeks later.
AK.expect: Partial first-choice results overnight; final result after the ranked-choice count.
